body:
### Problem

strdisplaywidth('ทำ') returns 1, so neovim thinks 'ทำ' needs only 1 cell. But actually 'ทำ' cannot be drawn in 1 cell. SARA AM, 'ำ' (U+0E33) is a SpacingMark, so it takes its own space instead of stacking on top of the consonant. No Thai font can fit a consonant plus SARA AM into one cell.

### Solution

For each remaining codepoint in the cluster, if its boundclass is UTF8PROC_BOUNDCLASS_SPACINGMARK then add one cell to the width. The grid only stores two cells per cluster, so the width is capped at 2. Segmentation is not changed, so the cursor and selection still treat the cluster as one unit.

comment_data.body: This will lead to two `utf_cluster_spacing_cells()` calls.
Thanks. I fixed at both sites by hoisting to a local.
I don't know much about this domain. Is a comment this long truly necessary?
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -486,6 +486,67 @@ int utf_char2cells(int c)
   return 1;
 }
 
+/// Number of extra display cells needed by the spacing marks belonging to the
+/// grapheme cluster which starts at "p".
+///
+/// UAX#29 keeps a SpacingMark in its base character's grapheme cluster: Thai
+/// SARA AM (U+0E33), Devanagari and Bengali matras, Khmer and Tamil vowel
+/// signs. That is correct for segmentation -- the cursor should treat the
+/// cluster as one unit -- but it says nothing about display, and UAX#29 is
+/// explicit about that: "Default grapheme clusters do not necessarily reflect
+/// text display."
+///
+/// A spacing mark, by definition, advances the pen: part of its shape sits
+/// beside the base rather than above or below it. Giving the whole cluster a
+/// single cell makes it impossible to draw -- no Thai font can fit a consonant

comment_data.body:
This is not the place to write essays, a single reference like `see unicode version XX document YY section ZZ` is enough.

Also this file is not (no longer) about reflecting terminals. it is nvim's own (positive!) attempt at making sense at the unicode despite unicode considering "fixed grid text" a disgraced step-child. we already have quirkarounds in tui.c to handle terminal discrepancies. more logic/comments can be added there as needed.
comment_data.diff_hunk:
@@ -486,6 +486,67 @@ int utf_char2cells(int c)
   return 1;
 }
 
+/// Number of extra display cells needed by the spacing marks belonging to the
+/// grapheme cluster which starts at "p".
+///
+/// UAX#29 keeps a SpacingMark in its base character's grapheme cluster: Thai
+/// SARA AM (U+0E33), Devanagari and Bengali matras, Khmer and Tamil vowel
+/// signs. That is correct for segmentation -- the cursor should treat the
+/// cluster as one unit -- but it says nothing about display, and UAX#29 is
+/// explicit about that: "Default grapheme clusters do not necessarily reflect
+/// text display."
+///
+/// A spacing mark, by definition, advances the pen: part of its shape sits
+/// beside the base rather than above or below it. Giving the whole cluster a
+/// single cell makes it impossible to draw -- no Thai font can fit a consonant
+/// plus SARA AM into one cell, the narrowest known needs 119% of one -- so the
+/// mark ends up either scaled down until it is unreadable or clipped away
+/// entirely. It also desyncs Nvim from every wcwidth()-based consumer of the
+/// same text (tmux, zsh, ls, git) and from Vim, all of which count the extra
+/// cell. Terminals that do their own segmentation are split on this: Alacritty
+/// and Ghostty give the mark its own cell, kitty does not.

comment_data.body:
it is not about storage (we can store endless continuation cells), more like what consumers of expect. We might look at increasing this eventually but not in the 0.13 cycle.

"currently, the grid allows maximum two cells per cluster"

NOTE: just writing UTF-8 chars directly in a `'føøbär'` string is entirely legal and safe. There is no need to write a `\xFF` sludge for text and then the actual text in a comment. (but a comment for the logic of the decomposition is still fine, if that is instructive)

The entire point of these exercisesis that we support ""international text"" as just **text** in the first place. it is not "binary data" that the cat has somehow smuggled in.

comment_regular_data.body: Please read CONTRIBUTING.md and write PR bodies yourself from now on.

does this also fix https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/34733 ?
In case it does, a test with some half-with kana like `ｶﾞｷﾞｸﾞｹﾞｺﾞﾊﾟ` would be nice. 

If this improves a wide category of distinct script types, it increases the "bang-for-buck" value of making the mbyte.c model (which is a model we _own_, by necessity) more complicated.

> Please read CONTRIBUTING.md and write PR bodies yourself from now on.

I'm sorry. It is my fault that I hadn't read the AI-assisted section. I've rewritten the body and trimmed the comments too.

> ok, unforunately it doesn't as 0xFF9E and 0XFF9F is considered even more special.
> 
> It is tempting to still merge this plus this little addendum for 0.13:
> 
> ```diff
> diff --git a/src/nvim/mbyte.c b/src/nvim/mbyte.c
> index 5297b0d6ab..b7db583ace 100644
> --- a/src/nvim/mbyte.c
> +++ b/src/nvim/mbyte.c
> @@ -536,7 +536,8 @@ static int utf_cluster_spacing_cells(const char *p, int firstlen, int size)
>      }
>  
>      int c = utf_ptr2char(cur);
> -    if (utf8proc_get_property(c)->boundclass == UTF8PROC_BOUNDCLASS_SPACINGMARK) {
> +    if (utf8proc_get_property(c)->boundclass == UTF8PROC_BOUNDCLASS_SPACINGMARK
> +        || (c & ~1) == 0xFF9E) {
>        extra += utf_char2cells(c);
>      }
> ```
> 
> With the note that while this is not the general solution, it still fixes _some_ regression of thai and japanese (and some more) users in 0.13 .
> 
> As a more general solution, the `setcellwidth()` table (or a new sister table) will need to be queried for some broader but still reasonable subset of grapheme extenders, as the only way to for support conflicting terminal implementations (as well as just making the text look NICE like the specific user wants in some GUI:s which bends to the users will (where "some GUI:s" of course include some terminals which supports adapting to the program)).

Thanks. I added a test with your string and `ｶﾞｷﾞｸﾞｹﾞｺﾞﾊﾟ` is 12 cells now. The Thai and Devanagari cases are not affected.
